sideA.summary: Supplies are almost gone. The world is reconnected, and the remaining hope is a cure: reach Lake Baikal, find the PEARL lab, take what they made, and bring it to Johannesburg. There will not be another chance. Missing it this month loses everything.
sideA.text:
Our supplies are almost gone. We have come so close. We’ve reconnected the world. Now we hope to cure it. We must reach Lake Baikal, find the PEARL Lab, get whatever cure they have created, and bring it to Johannesburg.

We won’t have this opportunity again.

If we don’t do it this month, then all is lost.

sideB.summary: Archive, December, Year 70. Last note before the exodus to Utopia. The havens, the labs, and the writers all failed. They had hoped the Faded could hold the world together, and the havens end quietly. Those left behind will be lost. The world's fate is in Utopia's hands, and the writers march there for salvation.
sideB.text:
DECEMBER, YEAR 70

Final note before the exodus to Utopia. The havens failed. The labs did not do their jobs. We did not do ours. We had such hopes that the Faded could hold the world together. But the havens end "not with a bang, but with a whimper." I feel pity for those we leave behind on the havens. They will be lost without us but the fate of the world lies in our hands, not theirs. To Utopia we march.

To salvation.
sideB.footer: Keep papers like this in the reserve.

mechanics.whenRead: Next card after the December Stop (12-01), read while drawing through the first December setup.
rules: No board effect. The archive side says to keep papers like this in the reserve.
The journal names the route the last objective uses: Lake Baikal and the PEARL lab, then Johannesburg.
mechanics.notes: Side B quotes the havens ending "not with a bang, but with a whimper." The signature is illegible. Flavor above is paraphrased. The journal does not itself reveal Baikal or grant the delivery.
